itakeit
How it works Setup Usage GitHub

Task tracking in Slack threads. Dead simple.

itakeit turns every message in one Slack channel into a task. People take it with 🙋, set the status with reactions, and a pinned board shows what is open. The work is tracked where you already talk about it.

Set it up View on GitHub

Self-hosted. One Docker container, one SQLite file, no public URL.

How it works

One dedicated channel. No forms, no extra tool, no context switch.

📝

Every message is a task

Post an issue in the channel. The bot replies in its thread with a status card.

🙋

Claim with one reaction

React 🙋 to take it. Several people can own a task. Remove the reaction to hand it back.

🚧

Status by emoji

Owners react 👀 investigating, 🚧 in progress, ⛔ blocked or ✅ done. The latest reaction wins.

❓

Ask the reporter

❓ pings the reporter in the thread. Their reply pings the owners and clears the status.

📌

A pinned board

One pinned message lists every open task with its status and owners, always current.

⏰

Nudges for stale work

Owners who go quiet on a task get a reminder in the thread after a configurable number of hours.

Setup

About ten minutes. You need a Slack workspace where you can create apps and a machine that runs Docker.

  1. Create the Slack app

    Open api.slack.com/apps, choose Create New App, then From an app manifest, pick your workspace and paste this manifest into the YAML tab.

    Show slack-app-manifest.yaml
    slack-app-manifest.yaml 
    display_information:
  name: I take it
  description: Claim issues with an reaction, track status in threads.
  long_description: Post a ticket in your channel. Users can claim it via reaction
    and share infos in thread. They update the status via reactions and receive reminders
    on stale tickets. No matter if there is an incident or just a very agile moving
    team. Track the work, where you communicate.
  background_color: "#1e8764"
features:
  bot_user:
    display_name: itakeit
    always_online: true
oauth_config:
  scopes:
    bot:
    - channels:history
    - groups:history
    - chat:write
    - reactions:read
    - pins:write
settings:
  event_subscriptions:
    bot_events:
    - message.channels
    - message.groups
    - reaction_added
    - reaction_removed
  interactivity:
    is_enabled: false
  org_deploy_enabled: false
  socket_mode_enabled: true
  token_rotation_enabled: false

    It requests only channels:history, groups:history, chat:write, reactions:read and pins:write.

  2. Get the two tokens

    Under Basic Information → App-Level Tokens, generate a token with the scope connections:write. That xapp-… token is SLACK_APP_TOKEN.

    Under Install App, install the app to your workspace and copy the Bot User OAuth Token. That xoxb-… token is SLACK_BOT_TOKEN.

  3. Prepare the channel

    Create a channel such as #itakeit (public or private), invite the bot with /invite @itakeit, and copy the channel ID from channel name → About. It looks like C0123456789.

  4. Write config.yaml

    Two lines are enough. Every other setting has a default. Emoji, reminder interval and board size are documented in config.example.yaml.

    config.yaml 
    channel: C0123456789
db_path: /data/itakeit.db

    The container runs as uid 65532, so the file must be readable by others: chmod 644 config.yaml.

  5. Run the container

    Export both tokens in your shell, then start the container from the directory that holds config.yaml.

    shell 
    export SLACK_BOT_TOKEN=xoxb-... SLACK_APP_TOKEN=xapp-...
    shell 
    docker run -d --name itakeit --restart unless-stopped -e SLACK_BOT_TOKEN -e SLACK_APP_TOKEN -v "$PWD/config.yaml:/config/config.yaml:ro" -v itakeit-data:/data ghcr.io/nice-pink/itakeit:latest
    Prefer Docker Compose?

    Put the tokens in a .env file next to it and run docker compose up -d.

    compose.yaml 
    services:
  itakeit:
    image: ghcr.io/nice-pink/itakeit:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      SLACK_BOT_TOKEN: ${SLACK_BOT_TOKEN}
      SLACK_APP_TOKEN: ${SLACK_APP_TOKEN}
    volumes:
      - ./config.yaml:/config/config.yaml:ro
      - itakeit-data:/data

volumes:
  itakeit-data:

    The log shows authenticated and connected to slack, and a board appears pinned in the channel. Post a message and react 🙋.

Run exactly one instance per channel. The container makes only outbound connections and needs no port. State lives in the itakeit-data volume, so it survives restarts and upgrades.

Usage

Reactions count only on the task message itself. Skin tone variants count as the base emoji.

WhoDoesEffect
anyoneposts a top-level messagenew task, status card in its thread, board updated
anyonereacts 🙋 on the taskbecomes an owner
ownerremoves 🙋stops owning it. When the last owner leaves, the task is unclaimed again, unless it is done.
ownerreacts 👀 / 🚧 / ⛔ / ✅sets the status. ✅ removes the task from the board.
ownerremoves the current status reactionstatus falls back to claimed
ownerreacts ❓reporter is pinged in the thread
reporterreplies while ❓ is setowners are pinged, status falls back to claimed
ownerreplies in the threadcounts as activity and resets the reminder clock
non-ownerreacts with a status emojiignored, with a private hint to claim first
